Advanced Features

This section collects the current advanced and developer-oriented workflows in RAPAS Photometry Pipeline.

Database Tracking System

RPP stores analysis-history metadata in SQLite so uploaded FITS files and generated ZIP archives can be tracked per user.

The tracking layer uses three linked tables:

wcs_fits_files
    Uploaded or generated FITS records tied to a user

zip_archives
    Result ZIP archives tied to a user

wcs_fits_zip_assoc
    Association table linking one FITS record to one or more ZIP results

This supports:

  • One FITS file associated with multiple processing runs

  • Per-user isolation of stored files and metadata

  • Automatic recording after successful result creation

  • Safe re-use of existing records when the same stored filename or archive is encountered again

Migrating Existing Databases

If you are upgrading an older deployment, use the migration scripts in scripts/.

python scripts/migrate_add_wcs_zip_tables.py --db-path /path/to/users.db
python scripts/migrate_legacy_db.py

The tracking-table migration creates a backup unless told otherwise and is designed to be rerunnable.

Inspecting Analysis History

The helper functions in src/db_tracking.py expose the recorded history:

from src.db_tracking import (
    get_fits_files_for_user,
    get_zip_archives_for_user,
    get_zips_for_fits,
)

fits_files = get_fits_files_for_user("alice")
archives = get_zip_archives_for_user("alice")
related_zips = get_zips_for_fits(wcs_fits_id=1)

Configuration Persistence

The frontend saves user settings as a single JSON blob and reloads it on the next login. The blob carries analysis_parameters (every sidebar control, including Max Magnitude Error mag_err_max and Detector Gain effective_gain), observatory_data and colibri_api_key.

  • Save: the Save Settings button in pages/app.py serializes the current dictionaries into the blob.

  • Load: pages/login.py restores the dictionaries into session state on login; any missing keys are filled from default_analysis_params in src/tools_app.py (both new controls are seeded there).

  • Backends: FastAPI (GET/POST /api/config) or the legacy Flask backend (GET /get_config / POST /save_config). See Backend API for the full comparison, payload shapes and storage columns.

Because the whole analysis_parameters dictionary is persisted verbatim, new sidebar controls round-trip automatically and require no database migration.

Development and Testing

Tests live in tests/ and are run with pytest from the project root (install the dev extras first with pip install -e ".[dev]"):

pytest

The configuration-persistence behaviour is covered by tests/test_config_persistence.py:

  • the FastAPI /api/config save/reload round-trip, including the 0 “disable the cut” / “automatic gain” values;

  • the legacy Flask /save_config / /get_config round-trip (skipped when Flask is unavailable, and run with a stub flask-cors when only the CORS extension is missing);

  • seeding of mag_err_max / effective_gain in default_analysis_params; and

  • structural checks that pages/app.py writes both controls into the saved dictionary and that pages/login.py restores analysis_parameters.

Both backend suites use an isolated SQLite database in a temporary directory, so running the tests never touches the developer’s users.db.

Transient Detection

The transient workflow is optional and runs after the main photometry and catalog-enhancement steps.

Candidate finding (src.transient.find_candidates) works as follows:

  • The user enables it from the Transient Candidates sidebar section and selects the reference filter.

  • The reference survey is chosen from the field declination: PanSTARRS in the north, SkyMapper in the south.

  • Sources are detected with SExtractor (via stdpipe) and cross-matched against the pipeline photometry catalog, taking the nearest counterpart within a seeing-based radius (the FWHM in arcsec, clamped to 1-4 arcsec). Matched detections receive the calibrated PSF magnitudes already measured by the pipeline.

  • When PSF photometry is unavailable - the columns are missing, or contain no finite value for the matched detections - the finder falls back to the calibrated 1.1 x FWHM aperture magnitude (aperture_mag_1_1 and its error) instead of aborting, so transient filtering still runs without an ePSF.

  • Detections flagged as unreliable (object/aperture truncated at the frame boundary, deblending overflow, degenerate centroid, or an all-masked / non-positive aperture) are discarded. These are SEP flag bits, so the mask passed to stdpipe is SEP_REJECT_FLAGS rather than stdpipe’s SExtractor-style default (0x7F00), which never matches raw SEP flags.

  • stdpipe.pipeline.filter_transient_candidates rejects detections that coincide with reference-survey or Vizier sources. The positional matching radius is half the seeing FWHM (set from fwhm and pixscale), and a coincident source is kept only when it is brighter than its catalog counterpart by more than mag_threshold (default 2.0 mag, after removing the median zero-point offset), i.e. when there is a genuine brightness excess.

  • Solar System objects are rejected separately through the SkyBoT service (120-second timeout), and candidates whose magnitude error is not finite are dropped.

  • No minimum S/N cutoff is applied to transient candidates. Low-S/N detections remain eligible if they pass the other catalog, known-source, and Solar System-object filters.

  • Cutouts (science and HiPS template) are displayed and saved for the top 20 candidates, ranked by signal-to-noise ratio.

This workflow should be treated as best-effort. Reference data, remote catalog services, and transient filtering may degrade gracefully when an external dependency is unavailable.

Astrometric Workflows

RPP supports several WCS-related paths:

  • Validation and reuse of an existing WCS already present in the header

  • Forced astrometry checks from the sidebar when the user wants a fresh solve attempt

  • Local blind solving through Astrometry.net and stdpipe

  • Optional refinement workflows when the local toolchain is available

If a new forced solve fails but the file already had a valid WCS, the frontend falls back to that valid solution so the rest of the pipeline can continue.

PSF Photometry

PSF photometry complements the aperture measurements and is useful when:

  • sources are crowded,

  • aperture measurements become unstable, or

  • a PSF-based comparison is desirable.

The pipeline builds an empirical PSF model from suitable stars and then reports PSF-derived fluxes and magnitudes alongside the aperture results when the fit is successful. Candidate stars are filtered on flux, S/N, shape, isolation and local-background flatness; the PSF is fitted in a compact region around each source while the ePSF itself is extracted from a larger cutout so its wings are preserved, and the aperture correction is derived from the exact model used for the fits.

After photometry the pipeline cross-checks the two methods: PSF and aperture sources are matched by position and the median psf_mag − aperture_mag is reported for each aperture. Because the aperture fluxes are placed on the same total-flux scale as the PSF (see docs/PHOTOMETRY_FORMULAS.md), the offset should be near zero; a median larger than PSF_APERTURE_CONSISTENCY_THRESHOLD (0.15 mag) raises a warning and the per-aperture diagnostics are stored in st.session_state["psf_aperture_consistency"].

The results view plots these offsets with plot_photometry_offsets: one panel shows the offset against the calibrated PSF magnitude with per-aperture median and zero lines, the other the offset histogram, and the figure is saved as <base>_psf_aperture_offset.png.

Custom Post-Processing

The generated CSV catalogs and ZIP archives can be reused in external scripts or notebooks for tasks such as:

  • light-curve construction,

  • differential photometry,

  • cross-run source aggregation,

  • custom filtering, or

  • publication-ready plotting.

For most programmatic entry points, prefer the modules summarized in api_reference.rst and the concrete pipeline helpers under src/.

Standalone Utilities

The scripts/ directory contains maintenance or utility scripts that are not part of the normal Streamlit button flow:

  • migrate_add_wcs_zip_tables.py

  • migrate_legacy_db.py

  • satellite_trail_detector.py

These are intended for administration, migration, or offline workflows rather than day-to-day frontend use.
